paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between training loss and the number of iterations for five different model configurations. The x-axis is labeled “#Iteration” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at 0.1 intervals. The first line, representing “Vanilla”, is purple with no markers and begins at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0, decreasing to approximately 2.45 at iteration 140,000 with a steep decline within the first 20,000 iterations, then leveling off. The second line, representing “StrmLLM (n=64)”, is orange with no markers, starting at approximately 3.3 at iteration 0 and decreasing to approximately 2.60 at iteration 140,000, also showing a rapid decrease at the start of training that slows over time. The third line, indicating “SepLLM (n=64)”, is green with no markers and begins at approximately 3.25 at iteration 0, falling to approximately 2.51 at iteration 140,000, with similar decrease behavior. The fourth line, indicating “SepLLM (n=64, H)”, is magenta with no markers and starts at approximately 3.2 at iteration 0, concluding at approximately 2.52 at iteration 140,000, mirroring the trend of the previous line. Lastly, the fifth line, representing “SepLLM (n=128)”, is navy with no markers, beginning at 3.15 at iteration 0 and finishing at approximately 2.55 at iteration 140,000, showing a comparable pattern of decline.
